title: Kipper and orange pâté on toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Kippers, oranges, butter, crème fraîche, horseradish, capers and bread are all ordinary larder and fridge foods.

supermarket.reason: Kipper fillets, oranges, crème fraîche and capers are everyday items at Tesco and similar shops.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a kettle, bowls, a fork, a knife, a grater and a toaster are needed, and the technique is simple.

works.reason: Softening 200g kippers in boiling water and mashing them with butter, crème fraîche and horseradish makes enough well-balanced pâté for eight slices of toast for four people.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is realistic for segmenting oranges, skinning and flaking the fish, mashing and toasting, and the five-minute soak matches the cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from the boiling water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Orange zest flavours the pâté and orange slices top each toast, a bright February pairing with smoky kippers.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with no restaurant jargon or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oily fish on wholemeal toast with fresh fruit is a satisfying, nourishing snack.
